limitations: Weak transfer evidence when the target structure is obvious from the task label.
Must not count as independent transfer if the transformation type reveals the target rule.
Errors must be plausible and unambiguous; deliberately broken English is not useful evidence.
Highly constrained prompts provide less transfer evidence than open contextual production.
Accepted-answer sets must cover all natural level-appropriate renderings; translation is an assessment mode, not a competence axis.
Items must not announce the grammar point being tested. Mixed grammar must sample genuine choice, not random juxtaposition.
Text difficulty, length and inference load must be controlled by the target year/CEFR profile.
Prompt scaffolding must not be so strong that the learner merely copies a template.
Scoring must separate task completion, comprehensibility, organisation, grammar and vocabulary rather than use one opaque correctness score.
Transcript access must follow the assessment policy; audio delivery must be level-appropriate and not artificially word-by-word.
The communicative situation must make the expected function clear without prescribing the exact wording.
Dialogue turns must be responsive and natural rather than mechanical grammar repetition.
Use only when oral performance is relevant to the learner's school programme or selected assessment profile.
Must report axis-level evidence as well as overall performance; an overall score must not hide a blocking weakness.
Only sample axes and outcomes required by the learner's actual school programme; do not force all catalogue content into every mock.

mode_rules: Assessment modes collect evidence for competence outcomes; they must never be treated as competence axes themselves.
A single task may collect evidence for multiple axes, but one primary axis must always be declared.
Recognition-only modes cannot by themselves satisfy a transfer requirement.
A cumulative test or recovery mock must preserve per-axis evidence so a high global score cannot automatically compensate for a critical required weakness.
